items.title: Kyle Whittingham says Michigan will not fire OC Jason Beck midseason: 'I'll evaluate everything after the season'
items.summary: ANN ARBOR, Mich. — For the third time in nine games, Michigan Wolverines football failed to score a single point in the first half. The Maize and Blue fell to Michigan State Saturday night, 15-6, barely avoiding its first shutout at home since 1967.

items.title: Michigan hits rock bottom versus MSU
items.summary: They didn’t score a touchdown. They didn’t need to. Michigan State’s 15—6 win over the Wolverines appeared predicated on the fact that if the Spartans scored 10 points, they’d win. Sadly, in this Twilight Zone of an autumn, that’s precisely how it played out.

items.title: DISASTER: List full of Losers as Michigan Gets Embarrassed on Their Home Field
items.summary: Michigan's offense was a disaster again. Their defense wilted against Michigan State's run game. Their special teams was a tire fire. As a result, Michigan gave up the Paul Bunyan Trophy.

items.title: Postgame Notes: Michigan vs. Michigan State
items.summary: Michigan's defense recorded four sacks against Michigan State, led by John Henry Daley's two-sack performance and Troy Bowles' career-high 15 tackles. Savion Hiter scored his third rushing touchdown of the season for the Wolverines.
